The *Dāsivimānavatthu* ("Servant Girl’s Mansion", Vv 18) is a canonical verse text located within the *Vimānavatthu* collection [SuttaCentral]. Centered on the karmic outcomes of ethical conduct, the text conveys the theme that wholesome and virtuous deeds lead to rebirth in the heavenly realms [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into five modern languages, including English [SuttaCentral].
Regarding textual reuse and parallels, the text is extensively cited and expounded in the commentary *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (exhibiting 54 matching units, particularly §1.1–16.4) and shares segments with the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (§14.1–16.4) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus records substantial verse-sharing with several other *Vimānavatthu* texts, most prominently *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Dīpavimānavatthu* (Vv 9), *Soṇadinnāvimānavatthu* (Vv 23), *Lakhumāvimānavatthu* (Vv 19), *Paṭhamasuṇisāvimānavatthu* (Vv 13), *Dutiyasuṇisāvimānavatthu* (Vv 14), *Tiladakkhiṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 10), *Tatiyanāvāvimānavatthu* (Vv 8), *Uttarāvimānavatthu* (Vv 15), and *Rajjumālāvimānavatthu* (Vv 50) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-linguistically, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with the Chinese *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100) and Tibetan texts including the *Saddharmasmṛtyupasthānasūtra* (D0287-2) and the *Gāthāsaṃgrahaśāstrārtha* (D4103), though these represent automated text-reuse matches rather than curated parallels [DharmaNexus].
